target.title: fix(sessions): auto-generate session titles via AI summarization
target.body:
Closes #77165
Related #89705

## What Problem This Solves

**Fix classification:** Root-cause feature completion for the generated session title path, plus a targeted CI expectation fix for the newly added test helper dependency.

**Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the concrete code/CI state after the focused validations below; product/privacy approval remains a maintainer decision because the feature sends bounded transcript excerpts only when explicitly enabled.

**Root cause:** Session rows only had manual names, first-message-derived fallbacks, or session-id fallbacks, and the generated-title work was incomplete unless the generated title was stored once, preserved through session listing/search/event/UI/tool projections, and suppressed whenever a user-provided title already existed.

Resolves a problem where users with many saved sessions had to identify sessions from truncated first-message text or session-id style fallbacks, making session history harder to scan and search.

The generated title also needs to behave consistently across the gateway session list, search, session-change events, Control UI filtering/patching, and the agent-facing `sessions_list` tool without overriding user-provided names.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Why this is root-cause fix:** The source of truth becomes durable session metadata (`autoTitle`) written only after enough direct user turns, and every consumer reads the same session-row title fields instead of recomputing or relying on one UI-only fallback. The stale-write guard checks the persisted `sessionId` before writing, so an async title generated for an old session key cannot leak into a newer session.

This adds an opt-in `sessionTitle` configuration and persists generated session titles as `autoTitle` metadata. Manual labels/display titles keep precedence, existing sessions without generated titles keep their current fallback behavior, and the feature remains default-off.

**Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `autoTitle` is owned by the session store, gateway rows expose it, gateway events clear it with explicit null sentinels, Control UI and `sessions_list` consume the gateway/session-row value, and reset/new/rollover paths clear generated titles without removing manual names.

The title is derived from the same stored metadata across gateway, UI, and agent-facing session list paths. Background title generation uses the session model/auth context, not a separate public SDK selector path, and the public plugin SDK runtime-auth helper only accepts public parameters.

**Related open PR / same-contract scan:** `Related #89705` is noted above; a read-only open-PR search for `77165 OR session title OR sessionTitle` returned no other open PR to defer to for the same generated-title contract.

**Patch quality notes:** The background title path intentionally swallows/logs title-generation failures because generated titles must not block user replies. Patch callbacks return `null`/`false` only to preserve existing session data when a session is missing, already manually titled, or no valid direct-user transcript text exists.

**Risk labels considered:** compatibility, auth-provider, security-boundary, session-state, availability, automation, and message-delivery.

**Risk explanation:** Compatibility risk is limited by default-off config and additive metadata. Auth-provider risk is limited to forwarding already-public runtime auth selector parameters and preserving public helper parameter typing. Security/privacy risk is limited by skipping manual/channel-titled sessions, filtering inter-session/tool-mediated provenance, bounding transcript input, and using the session's existing model/auth context. Session-state risk is limited by stale-write guards and reset/new/rollover cleanup.

**Why acceptable:** Users who do not enable `sessionTitle` keep existing behavior, and enabled users get one bounded background title write that does not affect reply delivery or activity ordering.

**What did NOT change:** Manual rename UI, migration/backfill for existing sessions, default-enabling generated titles, provider/channel/plugin capabilities, and the public PR template structure.

Out of scope: manual rename UI, migration/backfill for existing sessions, default-enabling generated titles, and new provider/channel/plugin capabilities.

## User Impact

When `sessionTitle.enabled` is on, users can get concise generated session titles instead of only first-message/session-id fallbacks. Session search can match those generated titles, already-open session lists can receive the post-write update, and agents using `sessions_list` see the same generated title users see.

Users who do not enable `sessionTitle` keep the existing behavior. Sessions that already have a manual `label`, `displayName`, or channel `subject` are not sent through the title model path.

## Evidence

**Behavior or issue addressed:** generated session title creation, persistence, list/search/event/UI/tool propagation, stale async write prevention, manual-title precedence, and the current CI failure in the test routing expectation.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `pnpm exec vitest --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts src/scripts/test-projects.test.ts --run`.

**Evidence after fix:** `ci-failing-test-projects` passed 1 test file / 83 tests after the `test-projects` routing expectation was updated for `src/auto-reply/reply/session-title-generator.test.ts`.

**Observed result after fix:** the previously failing Node shard assertion is now covered locally by the exact failing test file, and the PR branch remains a single commit.

**What was not tested:** I did not re-run the full repository validation or full `check:changed`; loopback-binding cases noted by local ClawSweeper can be sandbox-restricted. Remote CI is expected to re-run after submit.

**Target test file:** `src/scripts/test-projects.test.ts` for the CI failure, plus the generated-title focused tests listed below for the feature path.

**Scenario locked in:** importing `test/helpers/temp-dir.ts` now routes the new `session-title-generator.test.ts` through the auto-reply Vitest config, matching the CI sharding behavior.

**Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** the CI failure was an expected-plan mismatch, not a production-code failure; updating the routing expectation fixes the exact failing invariant without broadening the feature implementation.

Real local gateway proof after the generated-title patch:

```text
Validation `local-gateway-session-title-proof-final` (pass, exit_code=0, 92583ms):

[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=deepseek api=openai-completions model=deepseek-chat method=POST url=https://api.deepseek.com/v1/chat/completions timeoutMs=undefined proxy=env policy=custom
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=deepseek api=openai-completions model=deepseek-chat status=200 elapsedMs=543 contentType=text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
proof=local-gateway-session-title status=passed
agent.wait status=ok
session row key=agent:main:daily-fix-title-proof-1782883544408 autoTitle="TITLE PROOF OK" derivedTitle="TITLE PROOF OK"
sessions.list search="TITLE" matched=true matchedDerivedTitle="TITLE PROOF OK"
```

Focused validation after the async stale-write fix:

- `targeted-tests-after-async-title-race-fix` — passed 14 focused test files / 841 tests covering session-title generation, reset/rollover stale-title cleanup, post-reply notification, auth-boundary, gateway search/event payload, UI filtering/event patching, and agent-facing session list behavior.
- `typecheck-after-async-title-race-fix` — passed the core `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` check.
- `architecture-after-async-title-race-fix` — passed import-cycle, deprecated API/JSDoc, Kysely, and database-first legacy-store guards.
- `config-checks-after-async-title-race-fix` — passed config baseline and generated config schema checks.
- Local ClawSweeper commit review for `13968bcce773d6b145e1c186c64ba9031216db19` returned `result: nothing_found` / `check_conclusion: success`.

Additional validation after syncing with current `main` and resolving the merge conflict:

- `session-title-label-red` — failed before the fix because a session with manual `label` still reached transcript candidate resolution.
- `session-title-label-green` — passed 1 focused test file / 9 tests after `label` was treated as an existing title before transcript reads or title model calls.
- `config-docs-check-green` — `pnpm run config:docs:check` passed after regenerating `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` for the merged config surface.
- `plugin-sdk-api-check-green` — `pnpm run plugin-sdk:api:check` passed after refreshing `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256`.
- `plugin-sdk-surface-check` — `pnpm run plugin-sdk:surface:check` passed.
- `provider-auth-focused-tests` — passed 2 focused test files / 17 tests covering Plugin SDK provider auth and runtime model auth.
- `ci-failing-test-projects` — passed `src/scripts/test-projects.test.ts` through `test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts` after updating the test-project routing expectation for the new `session-title-generator.test.ts` temp-dir helper import.

Review finding mapping:

- RF-001: the prior `status: ⏳ waiting on author` signal is addressed by the current update and latest focused validation.
- RF-002, RF-004, RF-009, RF-010, RF-011: fixed by updating the `test-projects` routing expectation; `ci-failing-test-projects` passed 1 test file / 83 tests.
- RF-003: no additional code change; the existing local gateway proof above shows generated title metadata reaches `sessions.list` and search after the background write path.
- RF-005, RF-006, RF-007, RF-008: disclosed as maintainer decision/risk boundaries, not expanded into unrelated code changes. The feature remains opt-in/default-off, manual session names skip transcript/title generation, generated metadata is additive, and runtime-auth forwarding stays limited to public helper parameters.
